corpusSummary: The 2026 corpus comprises diverse social-science studies on large language models, spanning behavior, health, education, policy, and research-methods. It highlights tensions between algorithmic cognition and embodied human subjectivity, demonstrates AI-enabled benefits in learning and decision support, and foregrounds equity, safety, and transparency challenges in AI deployment, including misinformation, governance, and methodological validation of AI-inspired research workflows.

themes.name: LLM Cognition, Embodiment, and Critical Limits
themes.description: Papers investigate phenomenological framings of LLM cognition, compare algorithmic processing with embodied human subjectivity, and emphasize risks of anthropomorphism and gaps in situated knowledge.

themes.name: AI in Education, Literacy, and Learning Governance
themes.description: Research on AI-enabled tutoring, learning analytics, AI literacy across diverse learners, and governance/assessment implications, noting learning gains alongside risks of overreliance, ethics, and data privacy.

themes.name: AI as Research Tool: Methods, Validation, and Ethics
themes.description: The corpus demonstrates LLMs aiding coding, content analysis, sentiment analysis, and simulations, while underscoring the need for validation, transparency, energy considerations, and human oversight.

themes.name: Health, Equity, and Public-Policy AI
themes.description: Studies address equitable governance of digital health LLMs, safety and readability of patient information, misinformation mitigation, and AI’s role in public participation and ESG/policy decision-making.

emergingKeywords: AI as research tool and methodology
